title: Sequence by knowledge and by difficulty
statement: Sequence a course so knowledge and difficulty both progress, since ordering by standard or by readability alone left one of them flat.
example: A course organised by standard had all four units flat at about 900 to 913 on a reading-level scale.
detail: A coherence check on one course plan found no cross-unit difficulty escalation: all four units sat at about 900-913L because they were organised by standard (`grade3-reading/artifacts/LANE1_COURSE.md`). In another build, the assembly script grouped items by readability band and no knowledge progression existed (`grade3-reading/artifacts/g5_build_2026_07_02/g5_analysis_digest.md`), and a review called one course a readability staircase rather than a knowledge progression (`grade3-reading/artifacts/g5_build_2026_07_02/feedback_clean.md`).

evidence.quote: All 4 units are flat at ~900-913L average.
Units are organized by CCSS domain, not by difficulty progression.
groups by LEXILE band (830/920/1010L), not topic coherence; no knowledge progression exists
The course is sequenced as a Lexile staircase, not a knowledge progression
